criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then every tab is reachable and every card drills down one level.
Given sample mode, when any tab is shown, then the sample data is visibly labelled as sample.

Given the Command Center, when any tab renders, then .colaberry/plan.json and .colaberry/progress.json are both committed in this repo and every tab reads its content from them at runtime rather than from hard-coded values.
Given the Command Center, when any tab is shown, then .colaberry/manifest.json is committed in this repo and every tab shows how old that data is and warns when the age exceeds a week.
Trust — no tab shows a number, a connection or a result the project has not actually produced.
Given an order submission, when a duplicate order is detected, then log the detection.
Given an order submission, when no duplicate is found, then log the result.
Trust: All duplicate detections are logged for audit.

stories.notes: Walking skeleton: detectDuplicate() flags a duplicate on same customer + same items (order-independent) + submission within a 10-minute window, and logs the outcome either way via logEvent() for the audit trail. Both logging and detection throw rather than swallow on failure (malformed order, unwritable log path). 11/11 tests pass via `npm test`.

criteria.text: Given an action is taken, when it is logged, then it appears in the audit trail.
Given an action is taken, when logging fails, then an alert is generated.
Trust: All actions are logged with timestamps.

stories.notes: logEvent() already appended timestamped JSON entries to logs/audit.log and threw rather than swallowing write failures (built alongside STORY-001). Added raiseAlert(): on a write failure, logEvent now also appends an audit_log_write_failed entry (timestamp, original event, failure reason) to logs/alerts.log before re-throwing, so a logging failure leaves a durable, checkable alert instead of relying solely on the caller propagating the exception. Also covered the case where the alert write itself fails alongside the audit write: logEvent folds both failure reasons into the single thrown error rather than swallowing either. 13/13 tests pass via `npm test`.

criteria.text: Given a payment failure, when evidence is gathered, then it is stored for review.
Given a payment failure, when evidence gathering fails, then an alert is generated.
Trust: All evidence is logged with the issue details.

stories.notes: Walking skeleton, built in three layers reusing STORY-001/002's patterns. detectPaymentFailure() mirrors detectDuplicate(): validates an order/payment record from the online data source, flags paymentStatus === 'failed', and logs the outcome either way (REQ-002). evidenceTable.js mirrors orderEventsTable.js: in-memory insert/getAll/reset, rejecting incomplete or malformed evidence (missing orderId/issueType, or a missing/empty evidence object) at insert time. gatherEvidence() orchestrates REQ-005: validates the payment failure carries enough data (orderId, customerId, failureReason) before building evidence -- an incomplete input is rejected as a collection failure without ever reaching storage; a well-formed record is assembled and stored via evidenceTable.insert (injectable via options.evidenceTable so a storage failure can be tested without touching the real table). Every outcome -- success, collection failure, or storage failure -- is logged to the audit trail with full issue details via the existing logEvent(), and both failure types additionally write a second logEvent() entry to the alerts log so the failure is discoverable even if the caller doesn't handle the thrown error; nothing is swallowed, both failure paths re-throw. 38/38 tests pass via `npm test`. logger.js, detectDuplicates.js, and orderEventsTable.js were not modified.

criteria.text: Given a payment failure, when an action is recommended, then it appears in the action list.
Given a payment failure, when no recommendation is possible, then a notification is sent.
Trust: All recommendations are logged with rationale.

stories.notes: Walking skeleton, reusing STORY-002/003's patterns. actionList.js mirrors evidenceTable.js: in-memory insert/getAll/reset, rejecting a row missing orderId/issueType/recommendedAction/rationale/a valid timestamp. recommendAction() maps evidence.failureReason through a small ACTION_MAP (card_declined, insufficient_funds, expired_card) to a recommended action + rationale, stores it via actionList.insert (injectable via options.actionList), and logs action_recommended with the rationale (REQ-006, trust criterion). Incorrect/malformed input is rejected before any lookup, logged as recommendation_failed, alerted, and re-thrown -- not swallowed. When failureReason has no mapping, that is treated as 'no recommendation possible': it logs recommendation_not_possible, sends a notification via notifier.js's sendNotification() (a durable append-only log write mirroring alerts.log, injectable via options.notify), then logs notification_sent and returns null. A storage failure or a notification failure is likewise logged, alerted, and re-thrown rather than swallowed. 52/52 tests pass via `npm test`. logger.js, evidenceTable.js, gatherEvidence.js, and detectPaymentFailure.js were not modified.

criteria.text: Given a recommended action, when risk is assessed, then it is displayed with the action.
Given a recommended action, when risk assessment fails, then an alert is generated.
Trust: All risk assessments are logged with action details.

stories.notes: Walking skeleton, reusing STORY-004's patterns and logger.js/notifier.js unchanged. riskLevel.js maps a recommendedAction (from recommendAction.js's ACTION_MAP) to a riskLevel + riskRationale via a small RISK_MAP; all three known actions (retry_payment_with_updated_method, notify_customer_to_add_funds, request_updated_card) are 'low' since none move money or change order state automatically. An unrecognized recommendedAction is never guessed as low: getRiskLevel() falls back to 'high' with an explicit rationale (the 'incorrect risk levels' failure path). riskAssessmentTable.js mirrors actionList.js: in-memory insert/getAll/reset, rejecting a row missing orderId/issueType/recommendedAction/rationale/a valid riskLevel/riskRationale/timestamp -- each stored row carries the action's own fields alongside its risk, so the risk is 'displayed with the action' in one place. assessRisk() validates the incoming action record, looks up its risk, stores the combined row (injectable via options.riskAssessmentTable), and logs risk_assessed with both the action details and the risk fields (REQ-007, trust criterion). Malformed input is rejected before any lookup, logged as risk_assessment_failed, alerted, and re-thrown -- not swallowed. A storage failure is likewise logged as risk_assessment_storage_failed, alerted, and re-thrown. 77/77 tests pass via `npm test`. recommendAction.js, actionList.js, logger.js, and notifier.js were not modified; STORY-006's approval workflow was deliberately left unbuilt.

criteria.text: Given a high-risk action, when approval is required, then a notification is sent to the approver.
Given a high-risk action, when approval is not obtained, then the action is paused.
Trust: All approval requests are logged with timestamps.

stories.notes: Walking skeleton, reusing STORY-004/005's patterns and logger.js/notifier.js unchanged. approvalTable.js mirrors riskAssessmentTable.js: in-memory insert/getAll/reset, rejecting a row missing orderId/issueType/recommendedAction/rationale/riskLevel/riskRationale/status/a valid timestamp. requireApproval() takes a risk-assessed record (from assessRisk.js, REQ-007): a non-'high' riskLevel bypasses approval entirely (logged as approval_not_required, returns status 'auto_approved'), since REQ-008 only scopes high-risk actions. A 'high' riskLevel record is inserted into approvalTable with status 'paused_pending_approval' -- that status IS the paused state (acceptance criterion 2); this story deliberately does not add a way to grant approval, so a high-risk action stays paused until a future story records a decision. After storing, a notification is sent to the approver via notifier.js's sendNotification() (injectable via options.notify), then approval_required is logged with the action/risk details and a timestamp (REQ-008, trust criterion). Malformed input is rejected before any lookup, logged as approval_workflow_failed, alerted, and re-thrown -- not swallowed. A storage failure is likewise logged as approval_workflow_failed, alerted, and re-thrown. A notification failure is logged as notification_failed, alerted, and re-thrown; a dedicated test confirms the approval request already stored beforehand still shows status 'paused_pending_approval' afterward, so a failed notification never un-pauses the action. 82/82 tests pass via `npm test` (5 new). assessRisk.js, riskLevel.js, riskAssessmentTable.js, recommendAction.js, actionList.js, logger.js, and notifier.js were not modified.

criteria.text: Given an action is taken, when the outcome is verified, then it is logged as successful or failed.
Given an action is taken, when verification fails, then an alert is generated.
Trust: All outcomes are logged with verification details.

stories.notes: Walking skeleton, reusing STORY-005/006's patterns and logger.js/notifier.js unchanged. outcomeTable.js mirrors approvalTable.js: in-memory insert/getAll/reset, rejecting a row missing orderId/issueType/recommendedAction/rationale/riskLevel/riskRationale/a valid outcomeStatus (success|failed)/verificationDetails/a valid timestamp. verifyOutcome() takes an approved action record (from requireApproval.js/assessRisk.js) and calls an injectable options.checkOutcome(record) -- defaulting to a stub returning 'success', since no real outcome-checking integration exists yet, the same injectable-callback pattern orderEventListener.js uses for options.process. A checkOutcome result other than 'success'/'failed' (or a thrown error) is never treated as success: it is logged as outcome_verification_failed, alerted, and re-thrown ('verification process failure'). The result is stored via outcomeTable (injectable via options.outcomeTable) before anything else; a storage failure is logged as outcome_logging_failed, alerted, and re-thrown, so an outcome is never silently lost ('incorrect outcome logging'). Only when the stored outcomeStatus is 'failed' is an alert notification sent via notifier.js's sendNotification() (injectable via options.notify); if that notification itself throws, it is logged as alert_failed, alerted, and re-thrown, with a dedicated test confirming the outcome row is already durably stored by that point ('alert failure'). Every outcome -- success or failed -- is logged as outcome_verified with full verification details (REQ-009, trust criterion). Decision confirmed with the requester before building: verified outcomes get their own table rather than extending the STORY-005 risk-assessment row, consistent with how requireApproval.js was built on approvalTable.js rather than mutating riskAssessmentTable.js. 89/89 tests pass via `npm test` (7 new). assessRisk.js, requireApproval.js, riskAssessmentTable.js, approvalTable.js, logger.js, and notifier.js were not modified.

criteria.text: Given an uncertain issue, when processing is paused, then a notification is sent to the agent.
Given an uncertain issue, when pausing fails, then an alert is generated.
Trust: All pauses are logged with issue details.

stories.notes: Walking skeleton, reusing STORY-006/007's patterns and logger.js/notifier.js unchanged. pausedIssueTable.js mirrors approvalTable.js: in-memory insert/getAll/reset, rejecting a row missing orderId/issueType/uncertaintyReason/status/a valid timestamp; a stored row's status is always 'paused_uncertain' and this story does not add a way to resume it, the same boundary approvalTable.js draws for 'paused_pending_approval'. pauseProcessing() takes a record the caller has already determined to be uncertain -- this story does not decide what 'uncertain' means, the same boundary requireApproval.js draws around 'high risk' (that determination is out of scope, left for a future story/caller). It validates the record, stores it via pausedIssueTable (injectable via options.pausedIssueTable) with status 'paused_uncertain', notifies the agent via notifier.js's sendNotification() (injectable via options.notify), then logs issue_paused with full issue details (REQ-010, trust criterion). Malformed input is rejected before any storage, logged as pause_failed, alerted, and re-thrown -- not swallowed ('pause functionality failure'). A storage failure while pausing is likewise logged as pause_failed, alerted, and re-thrown. A notification failure is logged as notification_failed, alerted, and re-thrown, with a dedicated test confirming the issue already stored as paused beforehand stays 'paused_uncertain' afterward -- a failed notification never un-pauses it ('notification failure'). Logging failure itself is handled by logger.js, which already raises its own alert on a write failure, the same way every other module in this pipeline relies on it. 103/103 tests pass via `npm test` (14 new). requireApproval.js, approvalTable.js, verifyOutcome.js, outcomeTable.js, logger.js, and notifier.js were not modified.

criteria.text: Given actions are prepared, when a summary is generated, then it is displayed to the agent.
Given actions are prepared, when summary generation fails, then an alert is generated.
Trust: All summaries are logged with action details.
Given an order issue, when resolved within 2 hours, then it is logged as timely.
Given an order issue, when resolution exceeds 2 hours, then an alert is generated.
Trust: All resolution times are logged for performance analysis.
Given an order is submitted, when the system receives the event, then it starts processing the order.
Given an order is submitted, when the system fails to receive the event, then it logs an error and retries.
Trust: Every order submission event is logged with a timestamp and status.

stories.notes: Walking skeleton: handleOrderSubmission() stands in for the order-submission trigger (no real queue/webhook yet) — a valid event is written to the in-memory order_events table (orderEventsTable.js) and the audit log with status 'received' then 'processing_started', calling an injected process() stub. A malformed event (e.g. missing orderId) is logged with status 'error' and retried up to maxRetries (default 3) before throwing rather than swallowing. A process() callback that throws is logged as 'processing_error' and re-thrown immediately, not retried. logger.js and detectDuplicates.js were not modified. 23/23 tests pass via `npm test`.

criteria.text: Given the online data source, when inventory levels fall below threshold, then the system identifies an issue.
Given the online data source, when inventory data is missing, then the system logs an error.
Trust: Every identified inventory issue is logged with details and timestamp.

stories.notes: Walking skeleton, reusing STORY-003/004's evidence-table pattern plus STORY-012's retry pattern. inventoryData.js stands in for the online data source: fetchInventoryData() returns a fixed catalog of Kashmir Craft products (productId, name, quantity, threshold, warehouse), with options.fail/options.data hooks so tests can force an unavailable or empty source. inventoryIssuesTable.js mirrors evidenceTable.js: in-memory insert/getAll/reset, rejecting a row missing productId/issueType/a non-empty details object/a valid timestamp. detectInventoryIssues() calls the data source through fetchWithRetries (capped attempts, explicit per-attempt timeout via Promise.race) -- exhausting retries or an empty response is logged as inventory_data_source_unavailable / inventory_data_missing, alerted, and thrown (REQ-003's 'data source unavailable' path). Each returned record is checked independently: a malformed record is logged as inventory_data_missing and alerted but does not abort the sweep, so the rest of the catalog is still checked; a record with quantity < threshold is stored in inventory_issues via table.insert (details + timestamp) and logged as inventory_issue_detected (REQ-003, trust criterion); a clean record logs no_inventory_issue_found. A storage failure is logged as inventory_issue_not_logged, alerted, and re-thrown rather than swallowed. dataSource and inventoryIssuesTable are both injectable via options, matching gatherEvidence.js's testing pattern. 67/67 tests pass via `npm test` (13 new). logger.js, evidenceTable.js, and detectPaymentFailure.js were not modified.

criteria.text: Given the online data source, when shipping times exceed expected duration, then the system detects a delay.
Given the online data source, when shipping data is incomplete, then the system logs an error.
Trust: Every detected shipping delay is logged with details and timestamp.

stories.notes: Walking skeleton, reusing STORY-013's inventory-issue pattern plus STORY-012's retry pattern. shippingData.js stands in for the online data source: fetchShippingData() returns a fixed set of Kashmir Craft shipments (orderId, carrier, shippedAt, expectedDurationDays, actualDurationDays, destination), with options.fail/options.data hooks so tests can force an unavailable or empty source. shippingDelaysTable.js mirrors inventoryIssuesTable.js: in-memory insert/getAll/reset, rejecting a row missing orderId/issueType/a non-empty details object/a valid timestamp. detectShippingDelays() calls the data source through fetchWithRetries (capped attempts, explicit per-attempt timeout via Promise.race) -- exhausting retries or an empty response is logged as shipping_data_source_unavailable / shipping_data_incomplete, alerted, and thrown (REQ-004's 'data source unavailable' path). Each returned record is checked independently: a malformed record is logged as shipping_data_incomplete and alerted but does not abort the sweep, so the rest of the batch is still checked; a record with actualDurationDays > expectedDurationDays is stored in shipping_delays via table.insert (details + timestamp) and logged as shipping_delay_detected (REQ-004, trust criterion); a clean record logs no_shipping_delay_found. A storage failure is logged as shipping_delay_not_logged, alerted, and re-thrown rather than swallowed. dataSource and shippingDelaysTable are both injectable via options, matching detectInventoryIssue.js's testing pattern. 73/73 tests pass via `npm test` (6 new). logger.js, evidenceTable.js, inventoryIssuesTable.js, and detectInventoryIssue.js were not modified.

criteria.text: Given a customer support screen, when I perform the primary action, then it completes in three clicks or fewer.
Given a customer support screen, when I attempt to perform an action that requires more than three clicks, then I receive a notification to streamline the process.
Trust: Every action performed is logged with the number of clicks for audit.
